notes: The run went fine. This is the disk itself, without any cache, as the yardstick for the caches: about 570 MB/s for large reads, 250 MB/s for large writes, and 12 MB/s (reads) and 4 MB/s (writes) for small random requests one at a time. Windows' own file cache still speeds up programs that use it (the "buffered" rows). After the simulated power cut the file system was clean and all flushed data had survived. Of 10,000 new small files that nobody flushed, 8,236 were intact, 1,066 incomplete and 698 missing. That is normal Windows behaviour: it keeps new files in memory for a few seconds.
